correctness.rationale: Auel–Singer's three listed representatives have unchanged coordinate ratios precisely for the claimed stabilizers: normalize p1 by B, p2 by C, and p3 by B. Their ratio fields are respectively Q(sqrt(2)), Q(sqrt(2),i) and Q(i). All sign changes and square symmetries are rational matrices, so every point in each geometric orbit has that same ratio field, and the three orbits are Galois-stable (the conjugates of each representative are coordinate sign changes). Dividing 128,64,64 by 2,4,2 gives 64,16,32 arithmetic orbits. Independently, /workspace/reproductions/5.py (Python 3, no dependencies) finds the eight triple intersections of the nine branch lines of the coordinate-square map to the plane of magic squares, and no higher concurrence. Locally on the chart of a nonvanishing coordinate, the nonzero square roots are étale; two transverse vanishing branch forms can serve as base coordinates, and a third makes a single diagonal quadratic equation in the three vanishing square-root coordinates with three nonzero coefficients. Thus only the triple points yield nodes. Each has 32 projective sign lifts; the normalized square classes give 128,64,64 nodes over the stated respective fields. This reproduces the census without assuming the published orbit counts. It does not determine the Galois action on the whole Picard lattice.
